title: Stars dancing above the VLT
caption: Dotted star trails over the Very Large Telescope, Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Dotted trails of starlight curve around the southern celestial pole above ESO's Very Large Telescope (VLT). Its four 8.2-meter Unit Telescopes dominate the scene, their movements turned into a seemingly frantic blur as they swung between targets through the night. One of the smaller Auxiliary Telescopes hides in the bottom left corner.

The picture combines 450 exposures of 20 seconds each, covering two and a half hours of apparent stellar motion. That motion is an illusion, because it is Earth, not the stars, that turns as time passes. One frame even caught a shooting star, a small streak above the Auxiliary Telescope.

The sky over Cerro Paranal, 2600 meters up in Chile's Atacama Desert, is so dark and clear that long photo sequences like this can be made without a single cloud getting in the way. The image is the work of Farid Char, a student at Chile's Universidad Católica del Norte.

understand.summary: This is a composite of 450 exposures of 20 seconds each, spanning two and a half hours, by Farid Char. The source does not publish camera or color-processing details.
understand.eye: An observer would see sharp stars and slowly turning telescopes, but combining the sequence turns the stars into dotted trails and the telescopes' motion into a blur.

alt: Dotted circular star trails above four large telescope enclosures blurred by motion, with a small dome at bottom left and a short meteor streak above it.
